# CUDA

<!-- Generated by bazel run //tools/docs/languages:languages_bin -- --write from cuda/lang.json and cuda/defs.bzl. Do not edit. -->

This page helps you build, test and check CUDA code with rules_dx.

## Quick start

`MODULE.bazel` sits at the root of your repository and lists the Bazel modules, meaning external dependencies, that your project uses. Add `rules_dx` to it:

```python
bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
```

Then let dx set up the rest, as in the [Quickstart](../../README.md#quickstart):

```sh
bazel run @rules_dx//dx/launch:dx -- init --apply
```

For a CUDA project, `MODULE.bazel` then looks like this:

```python
module(name = "my_project")

bazel_dep(name = "rules_dx", version = "<release>")
dx_licenses = use_extension("@rules_dx//core:extensions.bzl", "dx_licenses")
dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula", "visual-studio-build-tools"], terms_sha256 = {"cuda-eula": "d6de69eacd5644f0f84d2289a54d07d29017377d37ab28d0227b3df3509b1a60", "visual-studio-build-tools": "9284a30da91bfdf5c56a681a6c007a0376cec75f069596dc6d28c3218c9e23d3"})
```

A `BUILD.bazel` file declares targets: the libraries, binaries and tests that Bazel builds. This one is a small CUDA package from [`cuda/tests/consumer`](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/cuda/tests/consumer/BUILD.bazel):

```python
load("@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl", "cuda_library")

cuda_library(
    name = "my_project_cuda",
    srcs = ["kernel.cu"],
    gpu_archs = ["sm_89"],
    visibility = ["//visibility:public"],
)
```

Build and test everything. `//...` means every target in the repository:

```sh
tools/dx test //...
```

## Dependencies

### Library components

The pinned stanza declares cuBLAS 13.8.0.4, cuFFT 12.4.0.43 and cuRAND
10.4.4.72 next to the compiler components, from the CUDA 13.4.3
redistributable manifest. Bazel fetches an archive only when a target uses it
(cuBLAS 877 MB, cuFFT 249 MB, cuRAND 87 MB).

Depend on the pinned labels:

```python
cuda_library(
    name = "gemm",
    srcs = ["gemm.cu"],
    gpu_archs = ["sm_89"],
    deps = ["@rules_dx//cuda:cublas"],  # or :cufft, :curand
)
```

These targets fail unless the files come from the pinned redistributable. Never depend on `@cuda//:cublas`, which skips the
check, or on `@cuda//:cuda_headers` or `@cuda//:cuda_all_files`, which fetch
every component. The `cufft` and `curand` targets are tagged `manual`.

See `cuda/tests/fixtures/cublas`.

## Quality

### Warnings

nvcc warnings fail the build by default. `cuda_library`, `cuda_objects`,
`cuda_binary` and `cuda_test` pass nvcc these flags:

```text
-Werror=all-warnings,cross-execution-space-call
-Wreorder -Wdefault-stream-launch -Wmissing-launch-bounds
-Wext-lambda-captures-this --display-error-number
```

So give every kernel `__launch_bounds__` and every launch an explicit stream:

```cuda
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256) saxpy(int n, float a, const float* x, float* y);

saxpy<<<(n + 255) / 256, 256, 0, stream>>>(n, a, x, y);
```

On one target, set `warnings_as_errors = False` to keep the warnings but not
fail on them. To allow warnings in the whole repository, add this line to
`.bazelrc`:

```text
common --@rules_dx//config:warnings_as_errors=false
```

`copts` and `host_copts` may not hide warnings or relax device code. Analysis
fails on `-w`, `--disable-warnings`, `-Wno-*`, `--diag-suppress`,
`--expt-relaxed-constexpr` and `--use_fast_math`, also when passed to the host
compiler through `-Xcompiler`. Fix the code instead.

### GPU tests

```python
load("@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl", "cuda_test")

cuda_test(
    name = "saxpy_gpu_test",
    srcs = ["saxpy_gpu_test.cu"],
    gpu_archs = ["compute_89:compute_89,sm_89", "sm_120"],
    min_compute_capability = "8.9",
    min_driver = "13.0",
    deps = [":saxpy"],
)
```

A machine with a GPU declares it with three flags, for example in its `user.bazelrc`:

```text
common --@rules_dx//cuda:gpu_compute_capability=12.0
common --@rules_dx//cuda:gpu_driver=13.4
common --local_resources=gpu=1
```

- `gpu_compute_capability`: compute capability of the device, `X.Y`.
- `gpu_driver`: CUDA driver version of the machine, `X.Y`.
- `--local_resources=gpu=<n>`: number of GPU tests that run at once.

Set both `gpu_` flags or neither. Without them every GPU `cuda_test` is incompatible, so `bazel test //...` skips it.

```sh
bazel test //:saxpy_gpu_test --test_output=streamed
```

The test source implements `int dx_gpu_test_main(void)` from
`dx/gpu_check.h`. Run the kernels there, compute a CPU
reference, and record each comparison with
`dx_gpu_check(name, want, got, n, abs_tol, rel_tol)`. Pass `got = NULL`
when a kernel launch fails. Return 0.

Set `min_compute_capability` and `min_driver` on `cuda_test` to run it on a GPU. Set both.

- `gpu_archs`: required arch specs, as for `cuda_library`.
- `min_compute_capability`: lowest device compute capability, `X.Y`.
  It must be at least the lowest arch in `gpu_archs`.
- `min_driver`: lowest CUDA driver version, `X.Y`, from `13.0` to `13.4`.

The runtime version is always the pinned toolkit, 13.4.

Every GPU `cuda_test` gets the tags `requires-gpu` and `resources:gpu:1`.
It runs sandboxed and its result is cached. The declared device, the
minimums and the runtime version are inputs of the test.

Each run prints one `dx-gpu-facts: {...}` line and writes
`gpu_facts.json` to `bazel-testlogs/<package>/<name>/test.outputs/`
(as `outputs.zip` when Bazel zips undeclared outputs; pass
`--nozip_undeclared_test_outputs` for the plain file).
The file has the schema `dx.cuda.gpu_facts.v1` and records the status,
the reason, the declared versions and device, the driver, the runtime, the device
name, compute capability and memory, and every check.

| Status | Meaning | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pass` | Every recorded check is within tolerance. | 0 |
| `fail` | A check failed, no check ran, a declared value is missing, or the device or driver is not the declared one. | 1 |
| `unavailable` | A device is declared, but there is no GPU, no driver, or a CUDA call failed. | 1 |
| `unsupported` | The device or driver is below the minimum, or the runtime differs. | 1 |

When the status is not `pass`, the first stderr line is
`<status>: <reason>`.

## Toolchain

nvcc uses the hermetic clang as its host compiler. The build needs no CUDA
install and no GPU.

### Setup

The CUDA rules load from `@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl`. rules_dx declares the
pinned toolkit and the nvcc toolchain. Add this to the root `MODULE.bazel`:

```python
dx_licenses = use_extension("@rules_dx//core:extensions.bzl", "dx_licenses")
dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula"])
```

### Toolchain

rules_dx declares the pinned nvcc toolchain; a consumer adds no
`register_toolchains` line. The one tag a consumer adds is
`dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula"])`.

### Errors

| Message | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `dx_cuda: the CUDA Toolkit EULA (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html) is not accepted; add dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula"]) to the root MODULE.bazel` | Add the license tag to the root `MODULE.bazel`. |
| `dx_cuda: unknown license '<name>'; the only one is 'cuda-eula'` | Accept `cuda-eula`. |
| `dx_cuda: gpu_archs is empty; set gpu_archs, for example gpu_archs = ["sm_89"]` | Set `gpu_archs`. |
| `dx_cuda: arch '<arch>' is not supported by nvcc 13.4; supported: ...` | Use an arch from the list. |
| `dx_cuda: copt '<flag>' silences warnings or relaxes device code; fix the code instead` | Remove the flag from `copts`, `host_copts` or `cuda_copts` and fix the warning. |
| `dx_cuda: @rules_cuda//cuda:compiler is '<compiler>'; dx CUDA targets compile with nvcc only` | Remove the `@rules_cuda//cuda:compiler` setting. |
| `dx_cuda: the CUDA toolkit is not the pinned redistributable (nvcc at '<path>'); remove your own rules_cuda cuda.redist_json and cuda.toolkit tags` | Remove your own rules_cuda `cuda.redist_json` and `cuda.toolkit` tags. |
| `dx_cuda: the CUDA toolkit is <version>; dx CUDA targets need 13.4` | Use the versions from Setup. |
| `dx_cuda: no nvcc toolchain for this target; dx CUDA targets build for linux_x86_64, linux_arm64, windows_x86_64, windows_arm64` | Build for one of the listed platforms. |
| nvcc fails with `unsupported clang version!` | Move the stanza before `register_toolchains("@llvm//toolchain:all")`. |

## License

The CUDA Toolkit is licensed under the
[NVIDIA CUDA EULA](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html).
`dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula"])` accepts it for this build.
Only the root module's tag counts. Without it, fetching the CUDA redistributables fails. `cuda-eula` is the only license name.

Accepting the license here does not grant you one. You still need your own from NVIDIA.

## Rules

`load` brings rules into a `BUILD.bazel` file. Load the ones you use from `@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl`:

```python
load("@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl", "cuda_library", "cuda_binary", "cuda_test")
```

### `cuda_library`

```python
cuda_library(name, srcs, gpu_archs, hdrs = None, visibility = None, tags = None, target_compatible_with = None, rdc = False, **kwargs)
```

Minimal wrapper over rules_cuda cuda_library; gpu_archs is required and rdc enables relocatable device code.

### `cuda_binary`

```python
cuda_binary(name, *, srcs, gpu_archs, deps = None, hdrs = None, visibility = None, tags = None, target_compatible_with = None, rdc = False, cuda_copts = None, **kwargs)
```

Compiles .cu sources with nvcc and links them into a cc_binary; cuda_copts go to nvcc.

### `cuda_test`

```python
cuda_test(name, *, srcs, gpu_archs, deps = None, hdrs = None, visibility = None, tags = None, target_compatible_with = None, rdc = False, min_compute_capability = None, min_driver = None, env = None, data = None, cuda_copts = None, **kwargs)
```

Compiles .cu sources into a cc_test; min_compute_capability.

### `cuda_objects`

```python
cuda_objects(name, srcs, gpu_archs, hdrs = None, deps = None, visibility = None, tags = None, target_compatible_with = None, **kwargs)
```

Compiles .cu sources to relocatable device objects for the deps of an rdc cuda_library.

### `cuda_component_library`

Forwards one pinned CUDA library component after the pin check.

| Attribute | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `component` | `label` | yes | The rules_cuda component target, for example @cuda//:cublas. |
| `component_name` | `string` | yes | rules_cuda short name of the component. |

### `cuda_doc_shard`

```python
cuda_doc_shard(name, lib, package = "", **kwargs)
```

Declares the DocIr shard of one CUDA library.

## Tools and package files

dx runs these tools and reads these package files for CUDA:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Tools | `clang_format`, `clang_tidy`, `nvcc_syntax` |
| Ecosystems | none |
| Manifests | none |
| Lockfiles | none |

## Platforms

CUDA builds and tests on:

- Linux arm64
- Linux x86_64
- Windows arm64
- Windows x86_64

See the [support matrix](https://github.com/devhusdk/rules_dx/blob/main/docs/support-matrix.md).

On Windows, nvcc compiles with `cl.exe` from the hermetic Visual Studio Build Tools, so you don't set `--//cc:compiler`. `cuda_binary` and `cuda_test` build and link everything in them with `cl.exe`. Link a `cuda_library` into a `cuda_binary` or `cuda_test`: on Windows a `cc_binary` or `cc_test` only takes one under `--//cc:compiler=msvc`. Accept both licenses in the root `MODULE.bazel`: `dx_licenses.accept(ids = ["cuda-eula", "visual-studio-build-tools"])`.

`bazel coverage` reports CUDA on Linux only. The host side of a `.cu` file is
reported against that `.cu` file.

## API docs

`tools/dx docs` builds the API docs with `doxygen`; see [docs](../cli/commands/docs.md).

To declare a docs target yourself, load the rule behind it:

```python
load("@rules_dx//cuda:defs.bzl", "cuda_doc_shard")
```
